items.summary: An experiment was conducted using publicly available football data to build a Bayesian model for predicting expected goals ($\text{xG}$). The process involved calculating the likelihood of the data given the parameters, incorporating the priors, and determining the evidence to find the posterior distribution over the parameters. By comparing two competing models using this framework, the evidence successfully updated the prior belief to a high probability for one model over the other.
